chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Dizzy Gillespie's style and trumpeters of the time
summary: Dizzy played then as he does now; Shavers was closest, and Smith left New York before Ray Nance and Miles Davis arrived.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Now, when you came back... Well, actually, before we pass on from that, just going back to this Savoy Ballroom thing you did with Dizzy. What kind of style was Dizzy playing in?
Yeah. Heh-heh. Playing the same way. In fact, like he was playing it today.
Was there anybody else playing trumpet roughly like that?
No. Not that I knew of. Not around New York. The closest man to it was Charlie Shavers, I believe it was...
Yes, Charlie Shavers. Of course, them other boys
that came up with Duke later on... That was after I already left. Ray Nance and all of them.
Oh yes. What about Buddy Anderson with Jay McShann? Was he anything like in Dizzy's league?
I didn't know much about him. No, I didn't know much about him. And Miles Davis either. All them fellows, they all came up there after I left.
